scope: The actual cap-complement probability in the unrestricted sourced middle interior law now has an explicit local energetic upper bound. The local middle energy L_S consists of every plaquette incident to S, including all crossings, and the two endpoint kinetic energies on S. The complementary exterior action is constant in the same interior coordinates and cancels exactly from the normalized estimate. Positivity of L_S and the previously proved global symmetric action bound yield L_S(v)<=2*L_S(v0)+36*D(v0,v) for any field with the same exterior, without a small-field assumption. The quaternion chord triangle inequality gives L_S(v)>=D(v0,v)-K_S(v0,u)-K_S(v0,w). Outside the radius-epsilon product cap, D>=epsilon^2. The centered reference Haar Gaussian has the exact partition mass(36*beta)^|S|, and the existing actual SU(2) Gaussian mass bound gives a per-active-link inverse factor C(beta)=cap(36*(beta+1))=864*scalarPartition(0)/Gamma(3/2)*(beta+1)*sqrt(beta+1). Only the reference Gaussian is factored. For a continuous perturbation R with |R|<=M, the full unrestricted interior cap-complement probability is at most exp(|S|*log C(beta)+beta*(2*V_incident(v0)+3*K_endpoints(v0,u,w)-epsilon^2)+2*M). This is proved for beta>=0, any nonnegative cap radius and every fixed exterior. The actual two Wilson insertions have M=4 and hence cost exp(8); the extra transported source has M=6 and cost exp(12), including overlaps. The existing unrestricted covariance transfer now gives explicit two-source and three-source covariance bounds with these exponential terms instead of an unevaluated complement probability, under the previous patch-curvature hypotheses. An additional explicit background-energy condition 2*V_incident+3*K_endpoints<=epsilon^2/2 yields exponent |S|*log C(beta)+2*M-beta*epsilon^2/2. That stronger eligibility condition is not asserted for all retained backgrounds and does not follow from the old cap-curvature hypotheses. No exterior-volume or boundary-depth term is introduced. The local covariance bound still grows with patch size and has no separation decay; retained exterior-response and endpoint-response covariances, background coverage in the matching response-weighted norm, the distant sum, global lower coercivity and all continuum obligations remain open. All twelve full Clay requirements remain open.

actual_objects.L_S(v): Every incident spatial plaquette defect plus the two temporal endpoint kinetic costs on S.
actual_objects.C(beta): Actual SU(2) Gaussian inverse-mass cap evaluated at 36*(beta+1).
actual_objects.M: 4 for the two bounded Wilson sources; 6 including the transported source.
actual_objects.badMass: Actual unrestricted sourced interior Gibbs probability of the cap complement.

proved_results: The full middle action is exactly beta times the fixed exterior energy plus beta times L_S.
Global local-energy upper bound L_S(v)<=2*L_S(v0)+36*D(v0,v) from the existing symmetric action estimate and positivity.
Global local-energy lower bound L_S(v)>=D(v0,v)-K_endpoints(v0,u,w), and D>=epsilon^2 on the cap complement.
The centered reference Haar Gaussian has partition mass(s)^|S|; no factorization of the interacting measure is asserted.
Its actual partition is bounded below by exp(-|S|*log C(beta)), with C(beta) exactly proportional to (beta+1)*sqrt(beta+1).
For any continuous source perturbation bounded by M, badMass<=tailBound with the actual Gibbs normalizer.
The literal two-source and extra-source Wilson instances cost exp(8) and exp(12), respectively, including overlapping links.
Under backgroundCost<=epsilon^2/2 the exponent improves to |S|*log C(beta)+2*M-beta*epsilon^2/2.
The actual unrestricted two-source and transported-source interior covariance bounds now contain 20*tailBound instead of an uncontrolled complement-probability symbol.
next_attack: Bind backgroundCost and its eligible/ineligible split to the actual retained exterior and endpoint laws in the required response-weighted norm.
Choose an admissible patch covering or background selection; fixed cap curvature alone does not ensure enough unrestricted mass.
Obtain separation decay for patch response and both retained covariance terms, with the full endpoint message and sourced partition.
Supply the dyadic distant-sum estimate and prove the independent global lower coercivity on the physical time scale.
Keep continuum compactness, scaling, nontriviality and reflected nonzero source survival as separate full obligations.
not_inferred: All twelve full Clay requirements remain open; no continuum Yang-Mills construction or uniform physical mass gap is proved.

The new cap-complement bound is explicit but can exceed one on energetically ineligible backgrounds. The retained law has not been proved to give sufficient response-weighted coverage by eligible patches.
Small curvature defects on a fixed cap do not imply that the cap carries most unrestricted Gibbs mass. The new local background-energy cost is retained and must be controlled separately.
The previous cap covariance hypotheses are unchanged. Only after they and an adequate energetic margin hold is the new unrestricted covariance estimate quantitatively small.
The covariance bound grows with active patch cardinality and has no spatial-separation decay. It does not establish the dyadic far-sum premise.
Both exact retained covariance terms remain: spatial exterior responses inside the middle bridge and propagated endpoint responses. Their true partitions and messages remain in the measures.
The local kinetic lower energy bound is not a global lower coercivity or Poincare inequality for the physical transfer, including its center-even sector.
Existing stationary averaged bad-bridge estimates have not yet been connected to the new eligibility costs in the matching unrestricted source hierarchy.
Controlled physical coupling/time scaling, a suitable overlap margin, reflected compactness and nonzero continuum survival remain open.
No gauge-covariant Balaban block-RG construction, localized inverse decay estimate or full physical clustering theorem is claimed.
